tagline: From saguaro to fir in twenty-seven miles of switchbacks.
intro: From Tanque Verde Road on the northeast edge of Tucson the highway enters the Coronado National Forest and starts up Molino Canyon by switchbacks, gaining more than 6,000 feet in 27 miles. It sets out among saguaro, mesquite and cholla and arrives in fir and aspen on the cooler north slopes, which the Forest Service likens to driving from the deserts of Mexico to the forests of Canada.

Work began in 1933 and took 17 years, with labor from a federal prison camp set up at the foot of the mountain for the purpose. Frank Hitchcock, who pushed the road through, died in 1935, and it carries his name.

moments.title: Gordon Hirabayashi Recreation Area
moments.text: In the Second World War the road's prison camp held Japanese American internees who were made to work on the highway. In 1999 the site was named for one of them.

moments.title: Summerhaven
moments.text: The village once kept a six-hole golf links at about 7,800 feet, by one historian's account the highest in the world. The Aspen Fire of 2003 took more than 250 of its 700 homes.

moments.title: Mount Lemmon
moments.text: Named for the botanist Sara Plummer Lemmon, who reached the top by horse and on foot in 1881. An old Air Force radar base on the summit now serves astronomers.

practical: The Pima County Sheriff runs a road condition hotline for the highway at (520) 351-3351.
